name: Museum of Trade Ceramics
nameVi: Bảo tàng Gốm sứ Mậu dịch
kicker: Trade ceramics in a tube house
summary: A nineteenth-century tube house at 80 Trần Phú, opened as a museum in 1995, with 368 ceramics from the 9th to the 19th century. The house itself is the other exhibit: front, bridge, and back, with a sky well. It closes on the 15th of each month. The clock and the fee are check on arrival.
timeNeeded: A museum hour. Exact minutes are check on arrival.
heroCaption: The wooden house at 80 Trần Phú, balcony and shutters

notice.title: Closed on the 15th of each month
notice.body: The museum overview says the doors are open every day except the 15th, when the staff do their own work. It does not print a clock. The fee is the ancient-town ticket, which is check on arrival.

body: The museum is the two-storey wooden house at 80 Trần Phú. The heritage overview says it was set up by Decision 139/QĐ-VH of 2 October 1995, with help from Japanese specialists. The collection is 368 objects, from the 9th and 10th centuries through the 19th, found at archaeological spots in Hoi An. They are the trade ceramics of the years when ships from East Asia and Europe used the port.

The house is the other reason to go in. The overview describes a typical old-town plan: a front house, a back house, and a bridge section between them, with an open sky well in the middle and the kitchen at the rear. From the balcony you look down the street of tiled roofs. The objects are inside. The street is the frame on the way out.

The overview says the museum is open every day except the 15th of the month. It does not print an opening or a closing clock, so the hour is check on arrival. Museums are the extra landmark on the 120,000 VND combination ticket the centre described in 2026. From 10 August 2026 the city fee is 20,000 VND per building. Ask which one is on sale.

figures.caption: The street of tiled roofs from the museum
figures.alt: A view down a tiled Hoi An street from the Museum of Trade Ceramics balcony

gettingThere: Walk to 80 Trần Phú, in the ancient town. The overview does not print a minute count.

legs.heading: From the old town
legs.body: Walk along Trần Phú to number 80. The minutes depend on your lane.

closed: Closed on the 15th of each month. No weekly closing day is printed.
admissionNote: No separate price is printed for this building. From 10 August 2026, Da Nang Resolution 98/2026 sets 20,000 VND per person per building, the same for a Vietnamese and a foreign visitor. The heritage centre’s notices of 26 January 2026 and 16 March 2026 still describe an 80,000 VND ticket for the streetscape, Chùa Cầu or Miếu Quan Công, and two other works, and a 120,000 VND ticket when a museum and three other works are added. The March notice says one purchase can be used through the stay, up to three days. A May 2026 article says the town is an open neighbourhood and many people walk in without a ticket. Which desk is in force is check on arrival.
